# Sets

### Proposition (well-ordering)

*Every nonempty set X can be well ordered*.

Proof:

1.  Let X be non-empty, order it by inclusion. Let $\mathcal{C} = \{ x \in X: x \in E_i \}$ the collection $\{ E_i \}$ is a partially ordered collection of subsets of X. By Hausdorff maximal principle, there is a maximal linearly ordered subset of X, call it $E_{max}$, clearly $E_{max} \subseteq \{ E_i \}$ .
